If sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) in the last 3 days, adjust forecast downward by 1–2% for early horizon (1–7 days) to avoid over-optimism.  
If sentiment is consistently negative (≤-0.33) in the last 3 days, adjust forecast upward by 1–2% for mid horizon (8–15 days) to counteract bearish bias.  
If sentiment spikes to 1.00 in the last 2 days, increase forecast by 1–3% for late horizon (16–30 days) to reflect strong bullish momentum.  
If sentiment is mixed (0.00–0.33) in the last 3 days, apply a 0.5–1.5% downward bias to forecast for early horizon to smooth out volatility.  
If sentiment is negative in the last 3 days but true price rises sharply in the next 5 days, reverse the adjustment and add 2–4% upward bias for mid horizon.  
If sentiment is positive but true price deviates downward by >3% from forecast, reduce forecast by 1–3% for late horizon to align with market reality.
